topic: Introduction to directional divergence, spiral divergence, Dutch roll and controllability
syllabus_extract: Introduction to directional divergence, spiral divergence, Dutch roll and controllability.
specific_objectives: 14.2.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the functions of AFCS.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of AFCS block diagrams and stability charts; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: Define directional stability in simple terms.
What is the primary function of the rudder?
How does the AFCS assist the pilot in maintaining heading?

development.content:
Definition of Directional Divergence
Causes of Directional Instability
Role of Vertical Stabilizer
AFCS Heading Hold Function
Recovery from Divergence

Definition of Spiral Divergence
Relationship between Roll and Yaw
Spiral Stability Criteria
AFCS Roll/Yaw Coordination
Pilot Recognition of Spiral Mode

Definition of Dutch Roll
Coupled Yaw and Roll Oscillation
Damping Mechanisms
AFCS Yaw Damper Function
Control Effectiveness in Oscillation

summary_questions: Explain how the AFCS yaw damper mitigates Dutch roll.
Differentiate between directional divergence and spiral divergence.
Describe the pilot's role in managing controllability during oscillations.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the fundamental elements of the flight control system as discussed in LP 15, focusing on how they interact with AFCS to ensure controllability.

pft_rows.syllabus: Need and role of flight control system, fundamental elements of flight control system.
